title: Summer 1941: playing every night, marriage and Club Lincoln in Columbus
summary: Playing every night, the band takes summer trips, works the interracial Club Lincoln in Columbus alternating with Tiny Bradshaw, and Pillars marries.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: a tragic thing, see, playing every night. And '41 was the year that we took off, and when I got married, you remember?
We drove out East. We were gone about three weeks, weren't we?
Oh, yes, that summer. The summer of '41.

The summer of '41, we took the band to Columbus, Ohio and we played at a place called the Club Lincoln. We had a good-sounding band. And we played there twice during that summer. We played there early summer, then we went back and played late summer. Club Lincoln was a nice little club, there and they would have nice crowds on the weekends and during the week. It was interracial. It was in the a black neighborhood. And Tiny Bradshaw had a very popular band during that time. They would use our band for maybe three weeks and then bring Tiny Bradshaw's band in for three weeks. And we had a most enjoyable summer in Columbus, Ohio. I went away and got married. My wife and I, we drove on back to Columbus. We put her on a train and sent her on back to St. Louis, didn't we?
